title: Philosophy: Logic, Being, Knowledge and the Human Person
description: Twenty-unit professional-style philosophy formation spanning logic, ancient and medieval thought, metaphysics, epistemology, anthropology, ethics, political philosophy, modern and contemporary thought, science, AI and philosophy of religion.
creditNote: 42 internal Save One Soul formation credits (21 units × 2). Professional-style study only; non-accredited and not a university philosophy qualification.

units.title: Philosophy and the examined life
units.label: Professional-style formation
objectives: Define philosophy and its major branches.
Distinguish philosophical argument from rhetoric and mere opinion.
Use questions, definitions and reasons as basic philosophical tools.
paragraphs: Philosophy asks fundamental questions about reality, knowledge, goodness, personhood, language and rational justification. Its method is not simply collecting opinions; it tests claims through argument, conceptual analysis and dialogue.
Catholic intellectual tradition values philosophy because grace does not destroy nature and faith does not abolish reason. Philosophy has its own methods and conclusions even when it serves theology.

lectureSections.title: Professional study focus
paragraphs: This unit should be studied through primary texts where possible, careful reconstruction of arguments, and comparison with at least one serious objection. The goal is not memorizing names but learning to reason within the problem-space of philosophy and the examined life.
points: Define terms before evaluating claims
Separate historical description from your own argument
State the strongest objection fairly
Identify what follows and what does not follow from the conclusion

units.title: Logic I: propositions, inference and validity
units.label: Professional-style formation
paragraphs: Logic studies structures of good inference. A valid deductive argument is one in which true premises could not lead to a false conclusion; validity does not by itself establish that the premises are true.
Inductive arguments support conclusions with degrees of strength rather than necessity. Philosophical rigor requires identifying which kind of support is actually being claimed.

Scholastic disputation trains intellectual charity by stating objections strongly before replying. A good response often begins with distinction rather than dismissal.

units.title: Ancient philosophy: Presocratics and the problem of being
units.label: Professional-style formation
objectives: Explain early Greek questions about nature and change.
Relate cosmological inquiry to later metaphysics.
paragraphs: Presocratic thinkers asked what reality is fundamentally made of and how change is possible. Their proposals initiated a move from mythic explanation toward rational cosmology.
The contrast between Heraclitean flux and Parmenidean being shaped Plato and Aristotle. The enduring issue is how a thing can genuinely change while remaining intelligible as the same thing.

units.title: Aquinas: being, essence and existence
units.label: Professional-style formation
paragraphs: For Aquinas, creatures do not possess existence in the same way God does. In created beings essence and existence are distinct, while God is ipsum esse subsistens—subsistent being itself.
This metaphysics supports a doctrine of radical creaturely dependence without making God one being among others.

units.title: Philosophy of the human person
units.label: Professional-style formation
paragraphs: Philosophical anthropology asks what kind of being a human person is. Cartesian dualism, reductive materialism and Aristotelian-Thomistic hylomorphism provide contrasting models.
A hylomorphic account treats body and soul as principles of one substance, avoiding both reduction to matter and separation into two complete beings.

units.title: Freedom, action and responsibility
units.label: Professional-style formation

Natural law begins from practical reason's recognition of human goods and moral principles; it is not simply a list of Church rules imposed externally.

objectives: Analyze philosophical questions raised by AI.
paragraphs: Science is extraordinarily successful at empirical explanation, but scientism is a philosophical claim that only science yields genuine knowledge. That claim is not itself established by an experiment.

AI raises questions about intelligence, representation, agency, consciousness, responsibility and personhood. Functional performance should not be equated automatically with subjective experience or moral status.

units.title: Philosophy of religion and the problem of evil
units.label: Professional-style formation
paragraphs: The problem of evil asks how suffering and wrongdoing relate to belief in a good and powerful God. Logical versions claim contradiction; evidential versions argue improbability.
Responses include free-will defense, soul-making approaches, skeptical theism and Christological or eschatological perspectives. No abstract account should trivialize concrete suffering.

units.title: Catholic philosophical synthesis and capstone
units.label: Professional-style formation
objectives: Integrate logic, metaphysics, epistemology, anthropology and ethics.
Use Fides et Ratio to frame philosophy's relation to theology.
paragraphs: A mature Catholic philosophical formation does not treat philosophy as theology in disguise. It allows reason to follow its proper methods while recognizing that truth cannot finally contradict truth.
The capstone should present a clear thesis, define terms, reconstruct major positions fairly, defend an argument and answer objections.
